person: Hana Kowalczyk is 34 and runs a one-person shop from a studio behind her house in Oregon. She sells ceramics and linen goods on her own site and two marketplaces, plus a small side of wholesale orders to gift and home shops in Ohio, Kentucky and Texas. In September a state tax notice arrived asking her to back up three wholesale sales that had no tax charged. She has never handled resale certificates formally; she just collected whatever form a shop sent. She wants to know quickly whether this is a big-business problem or a small one, and she wants questions she can answer from memory.
stated_up_front: Hey, I got a scary letter from Ohio's tax department about three wholesale orders where I didn't charge tax, and I honestly don't know what paperwork I have. Can you check my shop orders, my certificate sheet and my email, and tell me what's missing? Keep it simple, I have orders to pack.

facts.about: How many wholesale buyers she has
facts.truth: About a dozen retail shops in total, and eight of them bought this year. Her biggest wholesale order was about $1,400.
It came by mail around 22 September 2026 from the Ohio Department of Taxation. It lists three sales and the answer is due 19 January 2027.

facts.about: The three sales the state listed
facts.truth: Birchline Home in Columbus for $1,240, Tallow & Thread in Cincinnati for $860, and Harbor Lane Goods in Dayton for $615. All three were shipped with no tax charged.
Harbor Lane mailed their certificate well after the sale, and she only found it in her inbox last week. She thinks it came in early October.
Prairie Dog Mercantile in Austin buys about $700 a quarter. They sent Texas's own resale certificate, and she doesn't want to bother them again.
Bluegrass Porch Supply in Lexington bought once for $520 with no tax. The state did not list that sale, and she believes they sent a form.
One Ohio shop, Lantern & Loom in Toledo, wasn't exempt. She charged them tax on a $310 order because they never claimed resale.
Maple & Moss in Cleveland last ordered in August 2025, so more than a year ago. They have since asked to reorder.
An Airtable sheet with one row per shop, and a column she fills in when a form arrives. She knows some rows are half-empty.
She signs everything herself. She wants to see any letter to a buyer or to the state before it goes.

unknowns: Whether a certificate that arrived after the sale still counts for the state
What the rules say about how many days she has to collect a certificate
Whether a shop that hasn't ordered in over a year needs a fresh certificate
Whether an emailed certificate with no signature line counts as complete
